recent_signals.headline: Named (31 Oct) in the leader's written statement as attending the first reported meeting of Mojtaba Khamenei with all three service chiefs (with Abdollahi and Hatami). No photograph, video or audio. (CLAIMED meeting; intel KIN-B2, DIP-A11)

No photograph, appearance or named action found 13–26 Oct (DIP desk searched). The SNSC/Rezaei and speaker channels carry the hard line in public; the IRGC spokesman Mohebbi claimed the June ship strikes were chain-of-command authorised (15 Oct). (ABSENCE; intel DIP-A8)

**IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi's Navy Day message (8 Oct; Tasnim/Press TV): 'no extra-regional power has the right to threaten, establish a hegemonic presence or interfere' in the Persian Gulf/Hormuz — 'the strategic red line of Islamic Iran'; repeated 12 Oct.** Public, institutional voice of the IRGC on the strait while the ship war ran at its peak. — CONFIRMED (statement).

NYT (13 Sep, REPORTED, multiple unnamed Iranian/IRGC officials): IRGC chief Ahmad Vahidi told an 'enraged' Pezeshkian he had neither authorised nor known of the 6–7 July attacks on three ships (incl. a Qatari LNG carrier) that ended the June MoU; the internal probe traced them to Hossein Taeb. Vahidi's command authority over hardline cells is therefore in question — a structural reason the US has no counterpart who can guarantee a ceasefire at sea.
